summary: Implemented a persistent workspace-scoped MCP registry and lifecycle API. Registration accepts only administrator-configured allowlist IDs, lifecycle mutations require a server-side administrator token, discovery records provenance-labelled schemas and risk metadata, revocation and failure disable tools immediately, and the OpenAI Agents runtime exposes only exact persisted read tools. Gateway and registry failures degrade to a model-only path with explicit telemetry and never forward credentials to API responses, model context, or telemetry.

risks: Tool side-effect classification is deterministic and name-based; P3-T2 must add explicit per-server and per-tool administrator policy before write, execute or external tools can be exposed.
The Docker MCP Gateway image remains tagged latest and should be pinned and scanned during P6-T1.
followUps: Live connect/discover smoke was intentionally not run because this worker was prohibited from calling the external GitHub MCP server or reading/creating .mcp.env. Run it after MCP_ADMIN_TOKEN and gateway secrets are configured.
P3-T2 can consume GET /api/mcp registrationOptions, servers and events; mutation requests use allowlistId/serverId only and require X-Conductor-MCP-Admin.
